2027-01-16.title: Second Saturday of Denha
2027-01-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Faith comes from what is heard
2027-01-16.verse: So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.
theo: In the synagogue of Capernaum the people are “astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.” The scribes quoted the teachers before them; Jesus speaks as the one whose word does what it says. A man with an unclean spirit cries out: “What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are, the Holy One of God.” Jesus rebukes the spirit: “Be silent, and come out of him!” and the man is set free. The crowd asks: “What is this? A new teaching, with authority!” In Denha we see that the word of Jesus is not mere advice but power: it drives out evil and makes people whole.

Paul explains how this word reaches every nation: “For one believes with the heart and so is justified, and one confesses with the mouth and so is saved.” And “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.” But no one can call on a Lord of whom they have never heard. Paul asks: “And how are they to proclaim him unless they are sent?” and answers with Isaiah: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!” Then he sums it up: “So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.” Our own faith came by hearing, through apostles, missionaries, parents and catechists who were sent. Now it is our turn: to open our mouths for Christ, to support those who are sent, and to let our feet carry the good news.
outline: Ask: who first told you about Jesus?
The heart and the mouth together.
Faith comes from what is heard, so someone must be sent.
“So faith comes from what is heard.”
live: Speak about your faith to one person this week, simply and gently.
Pray for a missionary, and give something to the mission work of your diocese.
2027-01-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, you teach with authority and your word drives out every evil. Let your word live in my heart and on my lips; free me from all that binds me, and make my feet beautiful in carrying your good news to others. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the word of Christ is first proclaimed and heard, and then he gives himself on the altar. The Lord who commanded the unclean spirit comes to dwell in us.

quick: Jesus teaches with authority, and evil obeys him.
We believe with the heart and confess with the mouth.
Faith comes from what is heard, so someone must be sent.
2027-01-16.action: Speak gently about your faith to one person this week.
2027-01-16.question: Has anyone ever heard about Jesus from my mouth?

family.explain: St Paul says that people can believe in Jesus only if someone tells them about him. The feet of those who bring the good news are beautiful!
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for those who have never heard of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Who told you about Jesus, and whom could we tell?”

illus: An old catechist in Idukki taught Sunday school for forty years. At his funeral the church was full of men and women who had once sat on his benches. The parish priest said: he never travelled far, but his feet were beautiful; half this parish first heard the good news from his mouth.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, speak your word with authority among us, and free us from every evil. Amen.
share: He taught them as one having authority (Mark 1:22). Do I let Jesus' word have authority over my life?
Be silent, and come out of him! (Mark 1:25). What needs to be silenced and driven out of my heart?
How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news! (Romans 10:15). Where is the Lord sending me?
pm.resp: Lord, speak, and set us free.
interc: For preachers and catechists, that they may proclaim the word with faith.
For missionaries, especially those from our Church serving far from home.
For those oppressed by evil, addiction or fear.
For those who have never heard the name of Jesus.
For our group, that our feet may carry the good news.
pm.close: Father, faith comes from what is heard. Open our ears to the word of your Son, and send us to speak it with love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, in the synagogue at Capernaum the people were astounded: Jesus taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes (Mark 1:22). His word does not only explain; it acts.

A man with an unclean spirit cries out: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. Jesus says: be silent, and come out of him! And the man is freed (Mark 1:24–25). Evil recognises its Master. The people ask: what is this? A new teaching, with authority!

St Paul tells us how this word reaches us: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved. But how can they call on one of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone to proclaim him? So faith comes from what is heard (Romans 10:13–14, 17).

Our faith came to us because someone was sent: an apostle, a missionary, a grandmother, a catechist. Now we are the ones sent. Let us believe with the heart, confess with the mouth, and let our feet carry the good news. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus' words are so strong that even bad spirits obey him! And somebody once told you about Jesus. This week you can tell a friend: Jesus loves you!

intro: Theme: “So faith comes from what is heard.”
The Word who speaks with authority, and the messengers who carry it.

sub: A word that does what it says.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
They were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
points.apply: Read the Gospel of the day each morning this week.

q: The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
But Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him!” And the unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying with a loud voice, came out of him.
points.apply: Bring to confession whatever still binds you.

q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
And how are they to proclaim him unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
points.apply: Pray for and support a missionary this month.

concl: Jesus' word has authority to free and to heal.
Faith comes by hearing, and we are sent to speak.
